page.overview:
What is Tarn Aeluin?

Tarn Aeluin, also called the Blessed, Tarn-aeluin, or simply Aeluin, was the name given by the Grey-elves and Edain to a small, clear blue mountain lake in the center of the highlands of eastern Dorthonion, of the entrance of the shallow pass leading to Ladros and heather, themselves surrounded by trackless and uninhabited forests and highland plains of heather. Slender silver-gray birches also grew on the lake's margin. Many standing stones intruded into Tarn Aeluin from the wide moorland that surrounded it.

It is said that "in days of old" Tarn-aeluin had been hallowed by Melian. at Tarn Aeluin. There they remained hidden until they were betrayed by Gorlim. The next morning, Beren returned to Tarn-aeluin only to find carrion-birds croaking in mockery in the alder trees.

Tarn Aeluin is a Sindarin name with an unknown meaning. It consists of the words tarn ("gate") and aeluin ("blue-mere" or "blue lake"). Aeluin may be a compound of ael ("lake, pool") and the adjective luin ("blue"). Alternatively, Tarn may simply be an archaic English word meaning "mountain lake".
